item.research_question: Which powder metallurgy processing route (CIP+sintering, HIP, swaging, or SPS) combined with subsequent deformation (HPT) yields a fully dense, single-phase HfNbTaTiZr high entropy alloy with refined microstructure and acceptable mechanical properties?
item.processing_route: Three initial powder types were used: (1) Elemental powders mixed for 10 h at 45 rpm, cold isostatically pressed (CIP) at 400 MPa, then sintered at 1400 °C for 16 h; (2) Mechanically alloyed (MA) powders milled for 42 h; (3) Gas atomized (AT) powders. Sintering was performed at 1400 °C for 16 h in vacuum. Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) was at 1400 °C for 2 h under 190 MPa. Swaging was at 950 °C with an envelope of beta-titanium alloy. Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) was at 1300 °C for 2 min under 80 MPa. High Pressure Torsion (HPT) was at room temperature with 2.5 GPa pressure and 15 revolutions.
item.test_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with 98.1 N load (ISO 6507); microstructure analyzed via LM, SEM (BSE mode), and XRD (Cu Kα); oxygen content measured by gas fusion; porosity determined by image analysis; positron lifetime spectroscopy used for defect characterization.
key_findings: Swaging of sintered specimens resulted in cracking and failure, preventing full densification.
SPS of mechanically alloyed (MA) powders produced a fully dense but brittle specimen with high oxygen content (~1.07 wt %).
SPS of gas atomized (AT) powder with low oxygen content (~0.12 wt %) resulted in a fully dense, single-phase bcc specimen.
High pressure torsion (HPT) of the AT-SPS specimen refined the grain size from ~50 μm to below 500 nm (0.5 μm).
The AT-SPS-HPT specimen achieved a hardness of 410 HV10 (Abstract) and 584 HV10 (Section 4.3), attributed to grain refinement and dislocation density exceeding 5 × 10^14 m^-2.
Samples processed via CIP followed by HIP exhibited significantly lower hardness (~150 HV10) due to incomplete dissolution of elements and lack of a single-phase random solid solution.
Oxygen content above 0.8 wt % caused a sharp increase in hardness due to the formation of HfO2 particles.
item.mechanism: The authors argue that oxygen contamination is the primary cause of embrittlement and prevents the formation of a single-phase random solid solution. The high oxygen content in MA powders leads to the formation of stable HfO2 oxides which cause brittleness. The single-phase bcc structure in the AT-SPS sample is attributed to the high cooling rate (~300 °C/min) during SPS, which suppresses the formation of secondary phases (bcc2 and hcp). Grain refinement and increased hardness in HPT-processed samples are caused by the formation of a high density of dislocations (>5 × 10^14 m^-2) and the presence of oxide particles in oxygen-rich samples.
item.limitations: Swaging caused specimen cracking due to brittleness likely induced by high oxygen content (~0.75 wt %) or inappropriate deformation temperature/strain rate. The MA-SPS-HPT specimen broke into pieces during HPT, making its results disputable. Samples prepared by CIP and HIP retained considerable porosity and chemical inhomogeneities. The low hardness of HEAP-HIP samples could not be fully explained, though porosity and phase composition were suspected factors.
item.future_work: The authors state that the possibility of hot deformation of the alloy with increased oxygen content cannot be excluded under suitable conditions (i.e., low strain rate, or higher processing temperature), but this possibility needs more detailed study.
quotes: The most promising result was obtained by SPS treatment of gas atomized powder with low oxygen content.

The microstructure of HfNbTaTiZr specimen prepared this way can be refined by high pressure torsion deformation resulting in a high hardness of 410 HV10 and very fine microstructure with grain size well below 500 nm.

It should be pointed out that the possibility of hot deformation of the alloy with increased oxygen content cannot be excluded under suitable conditions (i.e., low strain rate, or higher processing temperature), but this possibility needs more detailed study.
